explanation: Keeping shoes on indoors is actually the French norm — hosts rarely ask guests to remove them, especially in a home you don't know well, and doing so unprompted can feel presumptuous. That said, many French people remove their own shoes inside their own home, so if you see a pile of shoes by the door, follow suit, and it's always fine to offer.
local_tip: Default to keeping your shoes on unless your host asks you to remove them or you notice other shoes already lined up at the door.

also_check.note: Removing shoes before stepping up from the genkan entryway is mandatory, not optional.
Removing shoes before entering a home is standard, basic etiquette, much like in Japan.
Generally not expected unless the host asks or the home clearly has a shoes-off household (e.g. light carpets, shoes piled at the door).
